reason: No server-side request is made anywhere in this code, so CWE-918 (SSRF) is inapplicable; the real weakness is user-controlled require/class instantiation (unsafe reflection / file inclusion, CWE-470/CWE-98), a different class than claimed.

subprocess.run(shell=True) is fed only from CLI argparse arguments and an env var of a local developer benchmark script, so the person invoking it already has shell access and there is no untrusted input boundary.

runCommand executes the admin-configured plugin command from CMPServerInitConstants.PluginConfig via exec.CommandContext with an argument vector (no shell), so no untrusted input is evaluated as code and CWE-94 does not apply.

This is the standard kubectl-style CLI plugin dispatch: it only runs argocd-prefixed binaries found on the local user's PATH (rejecting relative-path exec.ErrDot), executing software the user installed themselves, which is not code injection.

unserialize() reads a cache file that the same class previously wrote via serialize(), so the data is application-generated and locally trusted, not attacker-controlled input; without an attacker write path to the cache directory this is not exploitable deserialization.

The command passed to shell=True comes from the admin-authored event configuration (the code explicitly trusts admin config and intentionally allows shell semantics), so in the shown code there is no untrusted input reaching the shell.

Same self-written cache pattern: the file content being unserialized was produced by the class's own serialize() call, so the deserialized data is trusted local application state rather than attacker-controlled input.

This is a build-time script whose path inputs are the repository's own source file list (src/*.ts entrypoints), not external user input, so there is no untrusted data reaching path.resolve/writeFileSync and no path traversal exposure.

Duplicate of the same Cache.php read(): unserialize operates on a cache file the application itself serialized and wrote, so absent an attacker-controlled write to the cache location the CWE-502 finding is noise.
$_REQUEST['almox'] is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause with no casting, escaping, or parameterization, giving a textbook SQL injection reachable by any request parameter.
